@simonklee if you're already mid-fix, ignore me — otherwise here's what I found digging into this:

The burn isn't a stuck task, it's the status-bar spinner itself. `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/index.tsx` renders `<spinner interval={40} />` whenever `status().type !== "idle"`, and each tick fires `requestRender()` (opentui-spinner's `_advanceFrame`), which makes the opentui renderer re-render the entire scene graph. So a one-cell spinner drives 25 full-frame renders/sec, and each frame costs more than its 40ms budget on a long timeline — consistent with the ~15fps `writev` cadence and the CPU sitting between writes in the strace above.

It also keeps running while the timeline is static (long tool run, retry backoff), which matches the "no visible active output" observation.

I have a small fix ready (one file, ~20 lines in the prompt component): throttle the spinner to 400ms when no `message.updated` / `message.part.*` event has landed for 1.5s, keeping 100ms while streaming. Happy to open a PR against this issue — or if you'd rather keep it, the diagnosis is yours to use.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:

- #28175: [FEATURE]: Live session status panel in sidebar + background session completion notifications — covers completion notifications for background/parallel sessions
- #47479: [FEATURE]: notifications in the web UI — similar request for notifying when the agent finishes
- #43904: TUI: expose per-turn working/idle state in the terminal title — covers the terminal tab status marking part of this request (identifying which agent is running across multiple sessions)

Please review those issues and consider adding your +1 or additional context there if they cover your use case.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #43805: DeepSeek-v4-flash-free model missing from Zen provider dropdown despite existing in `/zen/v1/models` API — same symptom (account-enabled model absent from picker)
- #47120: Zen lists a model that OpenCode omits from its catalog and picker — same root cause (Zen API-advertised models not reconciled into the local catalog)
- #40524: Tracking issue for reconciling provider catalogs with `/models` endpoints

If your issue is distinct (e.g. the picker shows *wrong* models rather than simply missing ones, or the account-filtering aspect is new), please add a note clarifying how it differs so a maintainer can assess.

Decomposition of this issue into four independent causes with different fix paths:

**1. TUI animation render path (CLI/TUI, all platforms)**

The status-bar spinner (`packages/tui/src/component/prompt/index.tsx`, `interval={40}`) fires `requestRender()` per tick, and opentui's `CliRenderer.loop()` unconditionally calls `root.render()`, walking the full scene graph every frame. A one-cell animation therefore drives 25 full-frame renders/sec, with per-frame cost scaling with timeline size — the #42306 strace shows ~15fps `writev` with the CPU time spent between writes, i.e. per-frame cost exceeding the 40ms budget. Controlled measurements in this thread: @Raviu56 28.89% CPU enabled vs 1.40% disabled, @Astro-Han 24-43% enabled vs 1-5% disabled on a reversible same-PID toggle; 350ms spinner → 8.39%, confirming cadence as the controlling variable. Structural fix (dirty-region rendering) is upstream: anomalyco/opentui#1339. Throttling the spinner interval (400ms when no `message.updated`/`message.part.*` event has landed for 1.5s, 100ms while streaming) is being coordinated in #42306.

**2. FFF double-watch and index maintenance (macOS/Linux, scales with tree size)**

`packages/core/src/filesystem/search.ts` creates one `Fff.create({ basePath, aiMode: true, disableMmapCache: true, disableContentIndexing: true })` per location. fff maintains its own native background watcher and live index (`disableWatch` defaults to `false` and is not passed), so every tree is watched twice: fff's internal watcher plus opencode's `@parcel/watcher` (`filesystem/watcher.ts`). fff's API has no ignore-glob support, so `watcher.ignore` config does not apply to its watcher — consistent with @arcv's findings. CPU scales with tree size; `OPENCODE_DISABLE_FFF=1` removes the load (@arcv). Windows is unaffected because fff is disabled there by default (`flag.ts:34`).

Fix options:
- a. `disableWatch: true` + debounced `fff.rescan()` driven by opencode's own watcher events — single-watch architecture, at the cost of full rescans.
- b. `disableWatch: true` + accept index staleness between rescans (files created after boot missing from search).
- c. Defensive guard: `enableHomeDirScanning`/`enableFsRootScanning` are off by default in the fff API; passing them explicitly removes the dependency on fff defaults.

**3. Snapshot persistence → memory on session load (large monorepos)**

Full message snapshots including `summary.diffs` are persisted per `message.updated` event and loaded into memory when the session is opened. `"snapshots": false` disables this persistence and removes the load (@brandon-julio-t, @nhojb). Write-side retention is tracked in #33356; the read path is not covered by the open PRs there — `readAfter` in `packages/core/src/event.ts` loads an aggregate with `.all()`, unpaginated (#32005).

**4. Desktop GPU process (Electron)**

GPU-process render loop at idle; `prefers-reduced-motion` drops GPU 61% → 5% (@brandon-julio-t); tracked in #31664.

_The following comment was made by an LLM, it may be inaccurate:_

**Related PR found:**

- **#46260** - `fix(app): reveal scrollbar in settings dialog panels`
  - This is the same fix targeting the `dev` branch. According to the current PR description, #46260 could not be retargeted to `v2` because 11 of its 12 files don't exist on `v2` (settings UI was refactored from `packages/app/src/components/settings-*.tsx` to `packages/app/src/settings/<feature>/`). The current PR (48031) is a re-implementation of the same fix against the `v2` layout.

The PR notes that it supersedes #46260. These are intentionally separate implementations for different branches, not duplicates in the traditional sense, but they address the same issue on different code bases.

happening on v1.18.17
tried with 5.6 luna/high model

Confirmed on live traffic with 1.18.29, where the `?? 300_000` default is present and does not fire.

Provider `openai`, model `gpt-6-astra`, streamed subagent request.

Timeline of one stall:

- Request sent. Response headers received about 3 seconds later.
- No further bytes on that connection for 39 minutes.
- The session's last log line is the stream start. No later step, no error, no retry.
- The parent session stayed blocked behind the subagent for the whole period. The process was otherwise alive and still logging unrelated background work.

Socket state during the stall, the only established connection for that process:

```
ESTAB  ...:443   lastsnd:2355046  lastrcv:2352202
```

`lastrcv` is about 2.8 seconds more recent than `lastsnd`, so the headers arrived and the body then went silent.
No `chunkTimeout` was configured, so the request used the 300000 ms default.
It never fired, which matches the content-type condition described in this issue.
Recovery required killing the session by hand.

### There is a second copy of the same guard

`packages/core/src/aisdk.ts` has its own `wrapSSE` with the same content-type check, and it is also missing the default:

```ts
const chunkTimeout = options.chunkTimeout
...
if (!chunkAbortCtl || typeof chunkTimeout !== "number") return res
```

On that path nothing arms at all without explicit config, before the content-type check is even reached.
It special-cases `@ai-sdk/openai`, so openai traffic can reach it.
#47621 changes only `packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts`, so this copy keeps the gate.
That overlaps #46692.

I could not determine from the logs which of the two paths served the stalled request.
Both are consistent with what I observed.

### What I have tested

Locally I removed the content-type check in both copies and gave the `aisdk.ts` path the same 300000 ms default.
`bun test test/provider/header-timeout.test.ts test/provider/provider.test.ts` passes, 111 tests.

I have not yet observed a real stall under the patched build, so I cannot report that it catches this case in practice.

Hey, we’re going to remove `session.messageUpdate` in #48043. We added it too quickly without fully thinking through how it fits the session model—sorry for the back-and-forth.

Session history is intended to be append-only. Ideally, filtering tool or reasoning content from model input should happen through a context hook rather than by editing stored history. We’re also expanding session hooks across the main agent loop, transient generation (`generate`), title generation, and compaction.

We realize context hooks don’t address the database-size concern you raised, since they don’t delete stored content. Would dedicated database cleanup cover your needs—for example, opt-in automatic cleanup of older sessions after a configurable N days? Are there specific cleanup primitives you’re missing, or does your workflow require selectively deleting content within sessions you’re still using? Understanding that would help us design the right solution. If there’s a clear gap or broader demand, we’re open to revisiting this with a more deliberate design.
